Key points
• Anthropogenic climate change has resulted in elevated global mean ambient temperatures, CO2 concentration and
disturbed the World’s biogeochemical cycles. The consequences of these changes have been pervasive, resulting in direct and
indirect pathways. The direct pathways include the erraticism of weather-related events, which have intensiﬁed and become
more extreme. Indirect pathways include various insecurities to the dimensions of health, such as burdening socioeco-
nomic positions, risk for diseases, displacement, unaffordability of food, etc.
• Climate related adversities are responsible for the decline in agricultural yield and crop-loss, threatening food security in
